nodes.summary: The set of attributes mentioned by a selection condition, defined by recursion: it is empty for the always-true condition; for the comparison $a = d$ of an attribute $a$ with a constant $d$ it is $\{a\}$; for the comparison $a = b$ of attributes $a$ and $b$ it is $\{a, b\}$; for the negation $\neg \varphi$ of a condition $\varphi$ it is the set of attributes of $\varphi$; and for the conjunction…
nodes.title: Attributes of a selection condition

nodes.summary: For tuples $t$, $u$, $v$: $t$ and $u$ are compatible and the merge of $t$ and $u$ is compatible with $v$ if and only if $t$, $u$, $v$ are pairwise compatible, that is, $t$ and $u$, $t$ and $v$, and $u$ and $v$ are compatible.
nodes.title: Compatibility with a merge, grouped from the left

nodes.summary: For tuples $t$, $u$, $v$: $u$ and $v$ are compatible and $t$ is compatible with the merge of $u$ and $v$ if and only if $t$, $u$, $v$ are pairwise compatible, that is, $t$ and $u$, $t$ and $v$, and $u$ and $v$ are compatible.
nodes.title: Compatibility with a merge, grouped from the right

nodes.summary: Two tuples $t$ and $u$ are compatible (joinable) when they agree on every attribute where both are defined: for every attribute $a$, either $t$ is undefined at $a$, or $u$ is undefined at $a$, or $t(a) = u(a)$.
nodes.title: Compatible tuples

nodes.summary: The selection conditions over attributes $A$ and values $D$ are generated by: the condition that always holds; the equality $a = c$ of an attribute $a$ with a constant $c \in D$; the equality $a = b$ of two attributes $a$ and $b$; the negation of a condition; and the conjunction of two conditions.
nodes.title: Selection conditions

nodes.summary: Let $N$ be a set of relation names. A database schema assigns to each name $n \in N$ a finite set of attributes $\mathrm{sch}(n)$, and a database assigns to each name $n$ a finite set of tuples $\mathrm{db}(n)$. The database $\mathrm{db}$ conforms to the database schema $\mathrm{sch}$ when, for every name $n$, the set $\mathrm{db}(n)$ is a relation over $\mathrm{sch}(n)$.
nodes.title: Databases conforming to a schema

nodes.summary: Let $\mathrm{sch}$ be a database schema, assigning a finite set of attributes to each relation name. Two queries $e$ and $e'$ are equivalent with respect to $\mathrm{sch}$ when there is a finite set of attributes $S$ such that the inferred schemas of $e$ and of $e'$ with respect to $\mathrm{sch}$ are both $S$ (in particular both queries are well-formed), and $e$ and $e'$ evaluate to the same relation on every…
nodes.title: Query equivalence

nodes.summary: Given a database $\mathrm{db}$, which assigns a finite set of tuples $\mathrm{db}(n)$ to each relation name $n$, the value of a relational algebra query on $\mathrm{db}$ is the finite set of tuples defined by recursion on the query: the base relation $n$ has value $\mathrm{db}(n)$; for a query $e$ with value $v$, the selection $\sigma_c(e)$ by a selection condition $c$, the projection $\pi_T(e)$ onto a finite set…
nodes.title: Value of a query

nodes.summary: A well-formed query evaluates, on every conforming database, to a relation over its inferred schema.
nodes.title: Typing is sound

nodes.summary: Let $c$ be a selection condition, $t$ a tuple and $T$ a finite set of attributes containing every attribute of $c$. Then $c$ has the same truth value on the restriction of $t$ to $T$ as on $t$.
nodes.title: Selection conditions depend only on their attributes

nodes.summary: The truth value of a selection condition on a tuple $t$ is defined by recursion: the always-true condition holds; $a = c$ holds when $t$ is defined at $a$ with value $c$; $a = b$ holds when $t(a) = t(b)$ as possibly undefined values, so it also holds when $t$ is undefined at both $a$ and $b$; a negation holds when the negated condition fails; and a conjunction holds when both conditions hold.
nodes.title: Truth value of a selection condition

nodes.summary: The relational algebra queries over base relations named by $N$, with attributes $A$ and values $D$, are generated by: the base relation named $n$ for each $n \in N$; the selection $\sigma_c(e)$ of a query $e$ by a selection condition $c$; the projection $\pi_T(e)$ of a query $e$ on a finite set of attributes $T$; the natural join of two queries; the union of two queries; the difference of two queries; and the…
nodes.title: Relational algebra queries

nodes.summary: A finite set $r$ of tuples is a relation over the schema $S$, a finite set of attributes, when every tuple $t \in r$ is over $S$, that is, $t$ is defined exactly on the attributes of $S$.
nodes.title: Relation over a schema

nodes.summary: A tuple $t$ is over the schema $S$, a finite set of attributes, when $t$ is defined exactly on the attributes of $S$: for every attribute $a$, the value $t(a)$ is defined if and only if $a \in S$.
nodes.title: Tuple over a schema

nodes.summary: For all finite sets $r$, $s$ and $w$ of tuples, $(r \bowtie s) \bowtie w = r \bowtie (s \bowtie w)$, where $\bowtie$ is the natural join.
nodes.title: Associativity of the natural join

nodes.summary: For all finite sets $r$ and $s$ of tuples, $r \bowtie s = s \bowtie r$, where $\bowtie$ is the natural join.
nodes.title: Commutativity of the natural join

nodes.summary: If $r$ and $s$ are relations over the same schema $S$, that is, finite sets of tuples each over $S$, then their natural join is their intersection: $r \bowtie s = r \cap s$.
nodes.title: The natural join on a common schema is the intersection

nodes.summary: The natural join $r \bowtie s$ of finite sets of tuples $r$ and $s$ is the set of merges of $t$ and $u$ over all pairs of tuples $t \in r$ and $u \in s$ that are compatible, that is, agree on every attribute where both are defined. The merge of $t$ and $u$ takes the value of $t$ where $t$ is defined and the value of $u$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Natural join

nodes.summary: Let $r$ be a relation over the schema $S$ and $s$ a relation over the schema $S'$, that is, finite sets of tuples each over $S$, respectively each over $S'$. A tuple $t$ belongs to the natural join $r \bowtie s$ if and only if $t$ is over $S \cup S'$, the restriction of $t$ to $S$ belongs to $r$, and the restriction of $t$ to $S'$ belongs to $s$.
nodes.title: Membership in a join

nodes.summary: The merge of tuples $t$ and $u$ is the tuple whose value at each attribute $a$ is $t(a)$ if $t$ is defined at $a$, and $u(a)$ otherwise; it is undefined at $a$ when neither $t$ nor $u$ is.
nodes.title: Merge of two tuples

nodes.summary: Fix a database schema $\mathrm{sch}$ assigning a finite set of attributes to each base relation name. Let $e$ be a well-formed query with schema $S$, and let $T \subseteq T' \subseteq S$ be finite sets of attributes. Then the query $\pi_T(\pi_{T'}(e))$, the projection onto $T$ of the projection of $e$ onto $T'$, is equivalent to the query $\pi_T(e)$, the projection of $e$ onto $T$: both are well-formed with the…
nodes.title: Cascade of projections as a query rewrite

nodes.summary: Assume the set of attributes is finite. For finite sets of attributes $T \subseteq T'$ and every finite set $r$ of tuples, $\pi_T(\pi_{T'}(r)) = \pi_T(r)$, where $\pi_T$ is projection onto $T$.
nodes.title: Cascade of projections onto a subset

nodes.summary: Assume the set of attributes is finite. For all finite sets of attributes $T$ and $T'$ and every finite set $r$ of tuples, $\pi_T(\pi_{T'}(r)) = \pi_{T \cap T'}(r)$, where $\pi_T$ is projection onto $T$.
nodes.title: Cascade of projections

nodes.summary: For every finite set $T$ of attributes and all finite sets $r$ and $s$ of tuples, the projection onto $T$ of $r \cup s$ is the union of the projections onto $T$ of $r$ and of $s$: $\pi_T(r \cup s) = \pi_T(r) \cup \pi_T(s)$.
nodes.title: Projection distributes over union

nodes.summary: For a finite set $T$ of attributes and a finite set $r$ of tuples, the projection $\pi_T(r)$ is the finite set of the restrictions to $T$ of the tuples of $r$: $\pi_T(r) = \{ t|_T : t \in r \}$.
nodes.title: Projection of a relation

nodes.summary: For a permutation $f$ of the attributes and a finite set $r$ of tuples, the renaming $\rho_f(r)$ is the finite set of the tuples $t \circ f^{-1}$ for $t \in r$: each tuple keeps its values, and its value at an attribute $a$ moves to the attribute $f(a)$.
nodes.title: Renaming of attributes

nodes.summary: For a finite set $T$ of attributes and a tuple $t$, the restriction $t|_T$ is the tuple that agrees with $t$ on every attribute in $T$ and is undefined on every attribute outside $T$.
nodes.title: Restriction of a tuple

nodes.summary: Given a database schema assigning a finite set $\mathrm{sch}(n)$ of attributes to each base relation name $n$, the schema of a relational algebra query is either a finite set of attributes or undefined (the query is ill-formed), defined by recursion on the query: the base relation $n$ has schema $\mathrm{sch}(n)$; if $e$ has schema $S$, then the selection $\sigma_c(e)$ has schema $S$ when every attribute of the…
nodes.title: Schema of a query

nodes.summary: For all selection conditions $c$ and $c'$ and every finite set $r$ of tuples, selecting by $c'$ and then by $c$ gives the same result as selecting by $c$ and then by $c'$: $\sigma_c(\sigma_{c'}(r)) = \sigma_{c'}(\sigma_c(r))$.
nodes.title: Selections commute

nodes.summary: Let $r$ be a relation over a schema $S$, that is, a finite set of tuples each defined exactly on the attributes of $S$, and let $s$ be any finite set of tuples. If every attribute of the selection condition $c$ lies in $S$, then $\sigma_c(r \bowtie s) = \sigma_c(r) \bowtie s$, where $\sigma_c$ is selection by $c$ and $\bowtie$ is the natural join.
nodes.title: Selection pushdown into the left operand of a join

nodes.summary: Let $s$ be a relation over a schema $S'$, that is, a finite set of tuples each defined exactly on the attributes of $S'$, and let $r$ be any finite set of tuples. If every attribute of the selection condition $c$ lies in $S'$, then $\sigma_c(r \bowtie s) = r \bowtie \sigma_c(s)$, where $\sigma_c$ is selection by $c$ and $\bowtie$ is the natural join.
nodes.title: Selection pushdown into the right operand of a join

nodes.summary: Fix a database schema $\mathrm{sch}$ assigning a finite set of attributes to each base relation name. Let $e$ and $e'$ be well-formed queries with schemas $S$ and $S'$, and let $c$ be a selection condition all of whose attributes lie in $S$. Then the query $\sigma_c(e \bowtie e')$, the selection by $c$ of the natural join of $e$ and $e'$, is equivalent to the query $\sigma_c(e) \bowtie e'$: both are well-formed…
nodes.title: Selection pushdown as a query rewrite

nodes.summary: Assume the set of attributes is finite. Let $c$ be a selection condition, $T$ a finite set of attributes containing every attribute of $c$, and $r$ a finite set of tuples. Then $\sigma_c(\pi_T(r)) = \pi_T(\sigma_c(r))$, where $\sigma_c$ is selection by $c$ and $\pi_T$ is projection onto $T$.
nodes.title: Selection commutes with projection

nodes.summary: Assume the set of attributes is finite. Let $c$ be a selection condition and write $\sigma_c$ for selection by $c$. For finite sets $r$ and $s$ of tuples, $\sigma_c(r \setminus s) = \sigma_c(r) \setminus \sigma_c(s)$.
nodes.title: Selection distributes over difference

nodes.summary: Fix a database schema $\mathrm{sch}$ assigning a finite set of attributes to each base relation name. Let $e$ be a well-formed query with schema $S$, and let $c$ and $c'$ be selection conditions all of whose attributes lie in $S$. Then the query $\sigma_c(\sigma_{c'}(e))$, the selection by $c$ of the selection of $e$ by $c'$, is equivalent to the query $\sigma_{c' \land c}(e)$, the selection of $e$ by the…
nodes.title: Cascade of selections as a query rewrite

nodes.summary: Write $\sigma_c$ for selection by a selection condition $c$. For selection conditions $c$ and $c'$ and a finite set $r$ of tuples, $\sigma_c(\sigma_{c'}(r)) = \sigma_{c' \land c}(r)$: selecting by $c'$ and then by $c$ is the same as selecting once by the conjunction $c' \land c$.
nodes.title: Cascade of selections

nodes.summary: Assume the set of attributes is finite. Let $c$ be a selection condition and write $\sigma_c$ for selection by $c$. For finite sets $r$ and $s$ of tuples, $\sigma_c(r \cup s) = \sigma_c(r) \cup \sigma_c(s)$.
nodes.title: Selection distributes over union

nodes.summary: For a selection condition $c$ and a finite set $r$ of tuples, the selection $\sigma_c(r)$ is the set of tuples $t \in r$ on which $c$ evaluates to true.
nodes.title: Selection

nodes.summary: For a type $A$ of attributes and a type $D$ of values, a tuple is a partial assignment of values to attributes: a function that assigns to each attribute $a \in A$ either a value in $D$ or no value, in which case the tuple is undefined at $a$.
nodes.title: Tuple

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
